claim: A single presentation of a sugar reward to Drosophila activates distinct subsets of dopamine neurons that independently induce short- and long-term olfactory memories (STM and LTM, respectively).
source: A single presentation of a sugar reward to Drosophila activates distinct subsets of dopamine neurons that independently induce short- and long-term olfactory memories (STM and LTM, respectively).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior work establishing this finding.

claim: A recurrent reward circuit underlies the formation and consolidation of LTM.
source: In this study, we show that a recurrent reward circuit underlies the formation and consolidation of LTM.
evidence: This is the main finding of the study, supported by multiple experimental results presented in the manuscript.

claim: The feedback circuit is composed of a single class of reward-signaling dopamine neurons (PAM-α1) projecting to a restricted region of the mushroom body (MB), and a specific MB output cell type, MBON-α1, whose dendrites arborize that same MB compartment.
source: This feedback circuit is composed of a single class of reward-signaling dopamine neurons (PAM-α1) projecting to a restricted region of the mushroom body (MB), and a specific MB output cell type, MBON-α1, whose dendrites arborize that same MB compartment.
evidence: This anatomical description is supported by imaging data shown in Figures 1 and 2.

claim: Both MBON-α1 and PAM-α1 neurons are required during the acquisition and consolidation of appetitive LTM.
source: Both MBON-α1 and PAM-α1 neurons are required during the acquisition and consolidation of appetitive LTM.
evidence: This is supported by behavioral experiments using synaptic blockade shown in Figures 3 and 9.

claim: MBON-α1 additionally mediates the retrieval of LTM, which is dependent on the dopamine receptor signaling in the MB α/β neurons.
source: MBON-α1 additionally mediates the retrieval of LTM, which is dependent on the dopamine receptor signaling in the MB α/β neurons.
evidence: This is supported by behavioral experiments shown in Figures 6 and 8.

claim: A reward signal transforms a nascent memory trace into a stable LTM using a feedback circuit at the cost of memory specificity.
source: Our results suggest that a reward signal transforms a nascent memory trace into a stable LTM using a feedback circuit at the cost of memory specificity.
evidence: This is supported by the generalization experiments shown in Figure 10.

claim: A single presentation of nutritious sugar and an odor drives robust short-term memory (STM) and LTM in Drosophila melanogaster.
source: Appetitive olfactory learning in Drosophila melanogaster provides an opportunity to uncover the mechanisms underlying such integration of information, as a single presentation of nutritious sugar and an odor drives robust short-term memory (STM) and LTM, while non-nutritious sugar induces only STM (Krashes and Waddell, 2008; Colomb et al., 2009; Burke and Waddell, 2011).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior studies.

claim: Non-nutritious sugar induces only STM.
source: Appetitive olfactory learning in Drosophila melanogaster provides an opportunity to uncover the mechanisms underlying such integration of information, as a single presentation of nutritious sugar and an odor drives robust short-term memory (STM) and LTM, while non-nutritious sugar induces only STM (Krashes and Waddell, 2008; Colomb et al., 2009; Burke and Waddell, 2011).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior studies.

claim: Sugar reward is mediated by a group of dopamine neurons called the protocerebral anterior medial (PAM) cluster.
source: In Drosophila, sugar reward is mediated by a group of dopamine neurons called the protocerebral anterior medial (PAM) cluster (Burke et al., 2012; Liu et al., 2012).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior studies.

claim: Artificial activation of the PAM cluster neurons in the presence of odor drives robust appetitive STM and LTM formation.
source: Artificial activation of the PAM cluster neurons in the presence of odor drives robust appetitive STM and LTM formation.
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior studies.

claim: PAM-α1 is one of several cell types responsible for LTM formation.
source: Recent studies subdivided the PAM cluster neurons into STM- and LTM-inducing cell types and identified several cell types responsible for LTM formation, including PAM-α1 (Huetteroth et al., 2015; Yamagata et al., 2015).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior studies.

claim: The induced LTM is undetectable immediately after conditioning but gradually develops with time.
source: Interestingly, the induced LTM is undetectable immediately after conditioning but gradually develops with time (Das et al., 2014; Huetteroth et al., 2015; Yamagata et al., 2015).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior studies.

claim: Dopamine reward signals are conveyed by PAM cluster neurons to the mushroom body (MB), where the convergence of the reward and the odor is assumed to take place.
source: Dopamine reward signals are conveyed by PAM cluster neurons to a brain structure called mushroom body (MB), where the convergence of the reward and the odor is assumed to take place (Schwaerzel et al., 2003; Krashes et al., 2007; Trannoy et al., 2011; Cervantes-Sandoval et al., 2013; Huang et al., 2013).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior studies.

claim: The MB represents odors using a sparse subset of ∼2000 intrinsic neurons, Kenyon cells (KCs).
source: The MB represents odors using a sparse subset of ∼2000 intrinsic neurons, Kenyon cells (KCs) (Turner et al., 2008; Aso et al., 2009; Honegger et al., 2011; Campbell et al., 2013).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior studies.

claim: KCs send parallel fibers to form lobe structures, where multiple MB-output neuron (MBON) types elaborate spatially segregated dendritic arbors.
source: KCs send parallel fibers to form lobe structures, where multiple MB-output neuron (MBON) types elaborate spatially segregated dendritic arbors (Aso et al., 2014a).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to a prior study.

claim: The KC-MBON synapses are presumed to be modified in the course of memory formation by the reinforcing dopamine neurons.
source: The KC-MBON synapses are presumed to be modified in the course of memory formation by the reinforcing dopamine neurons (Tomchik and Davis, 2009; Gervasi et al., 2010; Sejourne et al., 2011; Cervantes-Sandoval et al., 2013; Placais et al., 2013; Boto et al., 2014).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior studies.

claim: The presynaptic terminals of PAM-α1 are localized to the basal compartment of the MB α lobe (α1).
source: The presynaptic terminals of PAM-α1 are localized to the basal compartment of the MB α lobe (α1) (Liu et al., 2012)
evidence: This is supported by citation and shown in Figure 1A,B,H.

claim: The dendrites of PAM-α1 stretch horizontally across the superior medial, intermediate, and lateral protocerebra (SMP, SIP, and SLP, respectively).
source: whereas the dendrites stretch horizontally across the superior medial, intermediate, and lateral protocerebra (SMP, SIP, and SLP, respectively) (Aso et al., 2014a; Yamagata et al., 2015) (Figure 1A,B,H).
evidence: This is supported by citations and shown in Figure 1A,B,H.

claim: One of the input candidates to PAM-α1 identified was the output neurons from the α1 compartment of the MB (MBON-α1).
source: Strikingly, one of the input candidates we identified was the output neurons from the α1 compartment of the MB (MBON-α1) (Figure 1C,D).
evidence: This is supported by computational search and shown in Figure 1C,D.

claim: The presynaptic terminals of MBON-α1 lie in close apposition to the dendrites of PAM-α1.
source: Transgenic expression of a presynaptic marker (Robinson et al., 2002) by MB310C-GAL4 revealed that the presynaptic terminals of MBON-α1 lie in close apposition to the dendrites of PAM-α1 (Figure 1E,I).
evidence: This is supported by imaging data shown in Figure 1E,I.

claim: The terminals of MBON-α1 were immunoreactive for the vesicular glutamate transporter.
source: The terminals of MBON-α1 were immunoreactive for the vesicular glutamate transporter (Figure 1F) (Daniels et al., 2008)
evidence: This is supported by immunohistochemistry shown in Figure 1F.

claim: MBON-α1 is glutamatergic.
source: The terminals of MBON-α1 were immunoreactive for the vesicular glutamate transporter (Figure 1F) (Daniels et al., 2008) but not for markers for GABAergic or cholinergic neurons (glutamic acid decarboxylase [Jackson et al., 1990] or choline acetyltransferase [Takagawa and Salvaterra, 1996], respectively) (Figure 1—figure supplement 1), consistent with MBON-α1 being glutamatergic (Aso et al., 2014a).
evidence: This is supported by immunohistochemistry shown in Figure 1F and Figure 1—figure supplement 1, and citation.

claim: MBON-α1 comprises two cells with very similar morphology.
source: Differential labeling of the individual MBON-α1 neurons in the same brain (Nern et al., 2015) revealed that MBON-α1 comprises two cells with very similar morphology (Figure 1G).
evidence: This is supported by multicolor flip-out imaging shown in Figure 1G.

claim: The processes of MBON-α1 and PAM-α1 substantially intermingled both in the SIP and SLP, and in the α1 compartment of the MB.
source: Confocal images revealed that the processes of MBON-α1 and PAM-α1 substantially intermingled both in the SIP and SLP, and in the α1 compartment of the MB—the input and output sites of PAM-α1, respectively (Figure 2A–E, Figure 2—figure supplement 1, Video 1).
evidence: This is supported by double-labeling confocal imaging shown in Figure 2A–E, Figure 2—figure supplement 1, and Video 1.

claim: Bouton-like structures of MBON-α1 are attached to the dendrites of PAM-α1.
source: To observe these processes in SIP and SLP in even greater detail, we employed a microscope with a super resolution detection system and found bouton-like structures of MBON-α1 attached to the dendrites of PAM-α1 (Figure 2B–D).
evidence: This is supported by super-resolution imaging shown in Figure 2B–D.

claim: A GRASP experiment revealed strong GRASP signals in SIP, SLP, and the α1 compartment, supporting the close juxtaposition between PAM-α1 and MBON-α1.
source: Furthermore, a GFP reconstitution across synaptic partners (GRASP) (Feinberg et al., 2008; Gordon and Scott, 2009) experiment using R72D01-LexA and MB310C-GAL4 revealed strong GRASP signals in SIP, SLP, and the α1 compartment (Figure 2F). This further supports the close juxtaposition between PAM-α1 and MBON-α1.
evidence: This is supported by GRASP imaging shown in Figure 2F.

claim: The blockade of PAM-α1 during conditioning did not significantly affect STM.
source: Consistent with our previous results (Yamagata et al., 2015), the blockade of PAM-α1 during conditioning did not significantly affect STM (Figure 3C)
evidence: This is supported by behavioral data shown in Figure 3C.

claim: The blockade of PAM-α1 during conditioning led to a severe impairment of sucrose-rewarded LTM.
source: Consistent with our previous results (Yamagata et al., 2015), the blockade of PAM-α1 during conditioning did not significantly affect STM (Figure 3C), but led to a severe impairment of sucrose-rewarded LTM (Figure 3D).
evidence: This is supported by behavioral data shown in Figure 3D.

claim: Blocking MBON-α1 during conditioning resulted in a preferential impairment of LTM.
source: Intriguingly, we found a similar preferential impairment of LTM upon the blockade of MBON-α1, using MB310C-GAL4 driver (Figure 3H).
evidence: This is supported by behavioral data shown in Figure 3H.

claim: Blocking MBON-α1 during conditioning did not significantly impair STM.
source: The same blockade did not significantly impair STM (Figure 3G).
evidence: This is supported by behavioral data shown in Figure 3G.

claim: Knocking down either dNR-1 or dNR-2 in PAM-α1 impaired LTM but not STM.
source: Intriguingly, knocking down either dNR-1 or dNR-2, which together form the functional NMDA receptor (Xia et al., 2005), impaired LTM (Figure 4C) but not STM (Figure 4B).
evidence: This is supported by behavioral data shown in Figure 4B,C.

claim: Thermo-activation of MBON-α1 in the presence of an odor induced appetitive LTM.
source: Indeed, we found appetitive LTM upon thermo-activation of MBON-α1 in the presence of an odor (Figure 5B).
evidence: This is supported by behavioral data shown in Figure 5B.

claim: Knocking down DopR1 in MBON-α1 did not significantly impair either appetitive LTM or STM.
source: On the other hand, knocking down DopR1 in MBON-α1 did not significantly impair either appetitive LTM or STM (Figure 6A and Figure 6—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: This is supported by behavioral data shown in Figure 6A and Figure 6—figure supplement 1B.

claim: Targeting wild-type DopR1 gene expression in KCs fully rescued the defects in dumb2 mutant flies.
source: dumb2 mutant flies showed severely impaired appetitive LTM. Targeting wild-type DopR1 gene expression in KCs fully rescued the defects (Figure 6B).
evidence: This is supported by behavioral data shown in Figure 6B.

claim: The blockade of the α/β KCs during conditioning significantly impaired appetitive LTM, but not STM.
source: Strikingly, the blockade of the α/β KCs during conditioning significantly impaired appetitive LTM, but not STM (Figure 7A,B)
evidence: This is supported by behavioral data shown in Figure 7A,B.

claim: When MBON-α1 was blocked only during the test phase of LTM, there was a severe impairment of conditioned odor approach.
source: Intriguingly, when MBON-α1 was blocked only during the test phase of LTM, we found a severe impairment of conditioned odor approach (Figure 8A).
evidence: This is supported by behavioral data shown in Figure 8A.

claim: The blockade of PAM-α1 during LTM retrieval did not have a significant effect.
source: In contrast, the blockade of PAM-α1 during LTM retrieval did not have a significant effect (Figure 8B).
evidence: This is supported by behavioral data shown in Figure 8B.

claim: Blocking any component of the feedback circuit for 1 hr immediately following conditioning resulted in a significant impairment of appetitive LTM.
source: Consistent with this idea, blocking any component of the feedback circuit for 1 hr immediately following conditioning resulted in a significant impairment of appetitive LTM (Figure 9A,C,E)
evidence: This is supported by behavioral data shown in Figure 9A,C,E.

claim: Blocking any component of the feedback circuit 22 hr after training did not impair appetitive LTM.
source: whereas the same blockade 22 hr after training did not (Figure 9B,D,F).
evidence: This is supported by behavioral data shown in Figure 9B,D,F.

claim: The performance decline is shallower in LTM compared to STM in odor generalization experiments.
source: Strikingly, the performance decline is shallower in LTM compared to STM (Figure 10C,D).
evidence: This is supported by behavioral data shown in Figure 10C,D.

claim: Compromised stimulus specificity in LTM is general.
source: We confirmed these results with another set of odorants, suggesting that compromised stimulus specificity in LTM is general (Figure 10—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is supported by behavioral data shown in Figure 10—figure supplement 1.

claim: MB output through MBON-α1 is required not only for the retrieval, but also for the acquisition and early consolidation of long-term appetitive olfactory memory.
source: Here, we extend the known role of MBONs and show that MB output through MBON-α1 is required not only for the retrieval, but also for the acquisition and early consolidation of long-term appetitive olfactory memory.
evidence: This is the main finding of the study, supported by behavioral experiments.

claim: Feedback signals from α/β KCs, mediated by MBON-α1, play a critical role in controlling the rewarding dopamine signals from PAM-α1.
source: These findings strongly support our model that feedback signals from α/β KCs, mediated by MBON-α1, play a critical role in controlling the rewarding dopamine signals from PAM-α1 (Figure 11).
evidence: This is an interpretation of the experimental results, supported by the data and shown in Figure 11.

claim: PAM-α1 might integrate simultaneous inputs from sugar perception and the nascent memory trace to augment and sustain the dopamine release to gate LTM formation.
source: More specifically, PAM-α1 might integrate simultaneous inputs from sugar perception and the nascent memory trace to augment and sustain the dopamine release to gate LTM formation (Figure 11).
evidence: This is a model proposed based on the experimental findings.

claim: The requirement of the NMDA receptor in PAM-α1 supports the model that PAM-α1 integrates inputs from sugar perception and the nascent memory trace.
source: The requirement of the NMDA receptor in PAM-α1 (Figure 4) further supports this model.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the experimental results shown in Figure 4.

claim: The reinforcing signal for LTM formation may depend on the presence of other sensory stimuli (e.g., odor).
source: In other words, the reinforcing signal for LTM formation may depend on the presence of other sensory stimuli (e.g., odor).
evidence: This is a speculation based on the proposed model.

claim: LTM formation is energetically costly.
source: As LTM formation is energetically costly (Mery and Kawecki, 2005; Placais and Preat, 2013; Musso et al., 2015), this gain control of the reinforcing signal might serve to restrict LTM formation to ecologically relevant situations.
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior studies.

claim: The dopamine release is likely to be sustained by the ongoing activity of the recurrent circuit.
source: The dopamine release is likely to be sustained by the ongoing activity of the recurrent circuit (Figure 9C–F).
evidence: This is an interpretation of the experimental results shown in Figure 9C–F.

claim: The output from α/β KCs during consolidation has an essential role for appetitive and aversive LTM.
source: A recent study reported a consistent finding that the output from α/β KCs during consolidation has an essential role for appetitive and aversive LTM (Huang et al., 2012) in addition to their role in retrieval (Krashes et al., 2007; Trannoy et al., 2011; Cervantes-Sandoval et al., 2013; Xie et al., 2013).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior studies.

claim: Appetitive LTM gradually develops after conditioning.
source: Recent studies revealed a gradual development of appetitive LTM after conditioning (Das et al., 2014; Huetteroth et al., 2015; Yamagata et al., 2015).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior studies.

claim: Ongoing activity in the recurrent loop may provide a circuit mechanism for the gradual LTM development.
source: Ongoing activity in the recurrent loop we propose here may provide a circuit mechanism for the gradual LTM development.
evidence: This is a speculation based on the proposed model.

claim: LTM consolidation in Drosophila requires post-training dopamine inputs.
source: In addition, previous studies reported that LTM consolidation in Drosophila (Placais et al., 2012; Musso et al., 2015) or in rats (Rossato et al., 2009) requires post-training dopamine inputs.
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior studies.

claim: Appetitive LTM is less specific to the trained odor, compared to STM.
source: Our generalization experiments show that appetitive LTM is less specific to the trained odor, compared to STM (Figure 10).
evidence: This is supported by behavioral data shown in Figure 10.

claim: Long-lasting memories are more generalized in mice and bees.
source: This result fits well into previous studies in mice and bees, demonstrating that long-lasting memories are more generalized (Stach and Giurfa, 2005; Wiltgen and Silva, 2007).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior studies.

claim: Distinct types of dopamine neurons signal reward for STM and LTM in the fly brain, and these memories are independently formed in different MB lobes.
source: In the fly brain, distinct types of dopamine neurons signal reward for STM and LTM, and these memories are independently formed in different MB lobes (Trannoy et al., 2011; Huetteroth et al., 2015; Yamagata et al., 2015).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior studies.

claim: Octopamine has been widely accepted as a positive reinforcement signal in insects.
source: Octopamine has been widely accepted as a positive reinforcement signal in insects (Hammer, 1993; Hammer and Menzel, 1998; Schwaerzel et al., 2003; Schroll et al., 2006; Perry and Barron, 2013).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior studies.

claim: In Drosophila, octopamine is considered to provide inputs to dopamine neurons that induce STM formation.
source: In Drosophila, it is considered to provide inputs to dopamine neurons that induce STM formation (Burke et al., 2012; Das et al., 2014; Huetteroth et al., 2015).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior studies.

claim: Memories with different temporal dynamics are mutually conflicting and formed in distinct areas in mammals, to which different classes of dopamine neurons project.
source: Recent studies in mammals reached a similar conclusion that memories with different temporal dynamics are mutually conflicting and formed in distinct areas, to which different classes of dopamine neurons project (Liljenstrom, 2003; Abraham and Robins, 2005; Kim and Hikosaka, 2013; Kim et al., 2014).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior studies.

claim: Independent processing of STM and LTM might be a conserved strategy among animals.
source: Independent processing of STM and LTM might be a conserved strategy among animals.
evidence: This is a speculation based on comparative observations.

claim: MBON-α3 (also known as MB-V3) mediates appetitive LTM retrieval.
source: Another type of MBONs also mediates appetitive LTM retrieval: MBON-α3 (also known as MB-V3) (Placais et al., 2013).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to a prior study.

claim: Blocking MBON-α3 during conditioning does not impair appetitive LTM acquisition.
source: In contrast to MBON-α1, blocking MBON-α3 during conditioning does not impair appetitive LTM acquisition (Placais et al., 2013).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to a prior study.

claim: Appetitive LTM formed in the α/β KCs is read out through at least two different classes of MBONs.
source: Therefore, appetitive LTM formed in the α/β KCs is read out through at least two different classes of MBONs.
evidence: This is an inference based on the experimental results and prior studies.

claim: MBON-α1 and MBON-α3 converge in the SIP and might activate shared downstream targets to guide conditioned odor approach.
source: These MBONs converge in the SIP (Aso et al., 2014a) and might activate shared downstream targets to guide conditioned odor approach.
evidence: This is a speculation based on anatomical observations.

claim: The recent comprehensive connectivity map of the afferent and efferent neurons of the Drosophila MB revealed many potential feedback connections outside the MB.
source: The recent comprehensive connectivity map of the afferent and efferent neurons of the Drosophila MB revealed many potential feedback connections outside the MB (Aso et al., 2014a).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to a prior study.

claim: Recurrent computation between learned information and reinforcement signals might be a fundamental principle of memory processing.
source: Considering the central role of the MB in sensory integration and memory-guided behavior (Aso et al., 2014b), recurrent computation between learned information and reinforcement signals might be a fundamental principle of memory processing.
evidence: This is a speculation based on the findings and prior knowledge.

claim: The activity of reinforcement neurons is modified upon associative learning in both vertebrates and invertebrates.
source: In both vertebrates and invertebrates, the activity of reinforcement neurons is modified upon associative learning (Hammer, 1993; Mirenowicz and Schultz, 1994; Riemensperger et al., 2005; Cohen et al., 2012; Schultz, 2013).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior studies.

claim: In the feedback circuit identified in this study, MBON-α1 mediates monosynaptic feedback to the dopamine neurons.
source: In this circuit, MBON-α1 mediates monosynaptic feedback to the dopamine neurons.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the anatomical and functional data.

claim: There is no monosynaptic feedback to the dopamine neurons found in mammals.
source: In contrast, there is no monosynaptic feedback to the dopamine neurons found in mammals, rather anatomical studies suggest such a feedback to be polysynaptic (Lisman and Grace, 2005; Watabe-Uchida et al., 2012).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior studies.

claim: A single association event can trigger formation of long-term memory (LTM) for environmentally relevant information, such as poison or food.
source: Environmentally relevant information, such as poison or food, can trigger formation of long-term memory (LTM) in a single association event (Garcia et al., 1955; Alexander et al., 1984).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior studies.

claim: It is advantageous for animals to refer to surrounding conditions when selecting what information to retain as stable LTM.
source: Because LTM formation is energetically costly (Mery and Kawecki, 2005; Placais and Preat, 2013), it is advantageous for animals to refer to surrounding conditions when selecting what information to retain as stable LTM.
evidence: This is an inference based on the energetic cost of LTM formation.
